request: True or myth? Five things everyone has heard, one at a time. #interactive #short
subtitle: Five things almost everyone has heard, from goldfish memory to radioactive bananas: true or myth? Guess each, then find out why.

spec.title: True or myth? Five things everyone has heard

sources.title: Lightning facts: the Empire State Building
sources.finding: the Empire State Building is struck about 25 times a year

sources.title: Banana equivalent dose
sources.finding: a banana's potassium-40 gives about 15 becquerels; the body keeps its potassium level constant

commands.speak: Five things almost everyone has heard. For each one: true, or myth?
First: you can see the Great Wall of China from space.

quiz.question: The Great Wall can be seen from space with the naked eye. True or myth?
quiz.right: Myth. The wall is long but only about as wide as a road, and China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, could not see it in 2003.

commands.speak: Next, the goldfish, said to forget everything in three seconds.

quiz.question: A goldfish's memory lasts only about three seconds. True or myth?
quiz.right: Myth. Goldfish remember for months: they learn when food comes, and which sound means dinner.

commands.speak: Then the old saying that lightning never strikes the same place twice.

quiz.question: Lightning never strikes the same place twice. True or myth?
quiz.right: Myth. Tall things get hit again and again: the Empire State Building is struck about twenty-five times a year.

commands.speak: Now the breakfast table: bananas are said to be radioactive.

quiz.question: Bananas are radioactive. True or myth?
quiz.right: True. A tiny share of their potassium is radioactive potassium-40, though your body keeps its potassium level steady, so it does no harm.

commands.speak: And last, the octopus, said to have three hearts.

quiz.question: An octopus has three hearts. True or myth?
quiz.right: True. Two hearts pump blood through the gills, and a third sends it round the body.

commands.speak: And the two that sounded silliest were true.

feedback.good: A sharp eye for a myth.
